title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, alerts, and roadmap (team wiki) - v2
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This page is the canonical platform engineering team wiki for systems and services, runbooks, dashboards, alerting standards, retrospectives cadence, and the near-term roadmap. It combines operational playbooks, how-tos, and links to reusable artifacts so engineers and oncall responders can find actionable procedures quickly.

Scope:
- Covers the core platform surface area: control plane services, ingress/routing, model-serving proxies, caching/KV, telemetry pipeline, autoscaling, and the platform observability stack (Prometheus/Grafana/Loki).
- Includes runbooks for the top incident classes, dashboard ownership and onboarding, alert SLO thresholds, and the 90-day roadmap.

Ownership

- Platform Engineering (primary): Builds and maintains the services and runbooks described here.
- Eng SRE (secondary): Owns alerting hygiene, oncall rotations, and postmortem facilitation.
- Observability Guild: Dashboard review and curator for company-wide templates.

Table of contents
1. Systems & Services overview
2. Platform how-tos (dashboards, onboarding, adding alerts)
3. Dashboards & alerting standards (SLOs and thresholds)
4. Runbooks: incident classes and step-by-step procedures
5. Retrospectives & continuous improvement process
6. 90-day roadmap & upcoming initiatives
7. Team wiki, onboarding, and links

1) Systems & services (high level)

Summary:
The platform is composed of the following logical services. Each entry includes owner, SLA targets, and critical metrics to monitor.

- Control plane API (service name: platform-control-api)
  - Owner: platform-api team
  - SLA: 99.95% availability (regional)
  - Critical metrics: 5xx_rate, request_latency_p95, error_budget_burn

- Ingress & routing (service name: platform-ingress)
  - Owner: networking & edge team
  - SLA: 99.9% for TLS termination and routing
  - Critical metrics: connection_errors, proxy_latency_p99, active_connections

- Model routing & variant selection (service name: router-service)
  - Owner: serving-runtime team
  - SLA: 99.9% availability for routing decisions
  - Critical metrics: fallback_rate, decision_latency_p50/p95, profile_mismatch_count

- KV caching (service name: prefix-cache)
  - Owner: serving-runtime/infra
  - SLA: eventual consistency; availability target 99.9%
  - Critical metrics: cache_hit_ratio, cache_evictions, write_errors

- Telemetry pipeline (Prometheus -> Thanos -> Grafana, logs -> Loki)
  - Owner: observability team
  - SLA: 99.5% data availability for 72h retention tier
  - Critical metrics: scrape_errors, ingestion_latency_seconds, alert_evaluation_time

- Autoscaler & capacity manager (service name: capacity-manager)
  - Owner: eng-sre
  - SLA: 99% for scheduled scaling operations; lower for reactive scale-ups
  - Critical metrics: scale_action_success_rate, queue_depth, pod_pending_seconds

2) Platform how-tos (concise, actionable)

A. Onboarding a new dashboard
1. Open the Grafana dashboard template repo: git@repo/grafana-templates.git
2. Create a new dashboard JSON from the canonical template: ./templates/platform-service.json -> dashboards/<service>-overview.json
3. Update variables: namespace, service_label, prometheus_datasource (use prometheus-thanos-prod)
4. Push branch and open PR with: ownership, short description, and the query justification (why these KPIs). Add Observability Guild as reviewer.
5. After merge, register dashboard in the dashboard-registry (docs + contact). Example command:
   - curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $DASH_API_TOKEN" -d '{"path":"/service/<service>-overview"}' https://dash-registry.internal/api/v1/register
6. Notify on #platform-dashboards Slack channel.

B. Adding a new alert rule (Prometheus alertmanager)
1. Confirm metric is instrumented and scraped (Prometheus target UP, no scrape_errors).
2. Draft rule under prometheus/rules/service_alerts.yaml using the standard template. Include:
   - expr: >-
       (query)
   - for: 5m
   - labels: severity: "sev2"/"sev1"
   - annotations: runbook_url, summary, runbook_steps
3. Open PR against prometheus-rules repo and add Eng SRE and Observability Guild as reviewers.
4. After merge CI will apply rules to the eval cluster; validate in staging and production canary.
5. Verify oncall receives an alert and that runbook link appears in the alert annotation.

C. Oncall escalation & handoff
- Primary oncall page: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
- Escalation matrix: primary -> secondary -> team lead -> eng-sre manager (detailed matrix in appendix).
- Handoff checklist: status, what was done, unresolved items, suggested next steps, and follow-up tasks in Jira.

3) Dashboards & alerting standards

SLOs and key thresholds (default company guidance for platform services)

| Service class | SLO (availability) | Burn window | Default alert threshold |
|---------------|--------------------:|------------:|-----------------------:|
| Control plane | 99.95% (monthly) | 7d | error_budget_burn_rate > 5%/hour (sev2) |
| Ingress/edge | 99.9% (monthly) | 24h | proxy_latency_p99 > 1200ms (sev2) |
| Routing | 99.9% (monthly) | 24h | fallback_rate > 0.5% (sev2) |
| Cache | 99.9% availability | 3d | cache_hit_ratio < 70% (sev3) |
| Telemetry | 99.5% data availability | 7d | ingestion_latency_seconds > 10s (sev2) |

Alert severity guidance:
- sev1 (page/phone): Service-down or data-loss impacting customers or All users - must page immediately.
- sev2 (oncall notice): Significant degradation of SLOs with potential customer impact. Page if sustained >15 minutes.
- sev3 (ticket): Non-urgent regressions or noise; create ticket in Jira and triage in the next sprint.

Alert hygiene checklist before raising new alerts:
- Is this actionable? (Can someone fix it?)
- Is the metric stable (not a counter reset) and correctly labeled?
- Do we have a runbook linked?
- Do we have an estimation for expected alert frequency?

4) Runbooks (incident classes and step-by-step)

Runbook naming convention: runbook-<service>-<incident-class>.md (stored in /runbooks repo and referenced from alert annotations).

Common incident classes (top of page quick links):
- Control plane 5xx spike
- Ingress TLS failures (certificate or CA rotation issues)
- Router fallback storms (large sudden fallback to lower-cost models)
- Cache pressure leading to evictions and increased latency
- Telemetry ingestion backlog/backpressure

Example: Control plane 5xx spike (runbook excerpt)
1. Triage (0-5 minutes)
   a. Check Grafana control-plane overview: 5xx_rate, request_latency_p95, pod restarts.
   b. Check service logs (Loki): query {job="control-api"} | json | level=error | last 30m.
   c. Verify deployment state: kubectl -n platform get deploy control-api -o wide.
2. Containment (5-20 minutes)
   a. If a recent deploy exists (last 30m), rollback: kubectl -n platform rollout undo deployment/control-api --to-revision=<previous>.
   b. Scale up replicas on healthy nodes if CPU is saturated: kubectl scale deployment/control-api --replicas=<n+2>.
   c. If DB connection errors, use DB failover plan (see appendix DB-runbook link).
3. Recovery (20m-2h)
   a. Deploy a canary fix to staging, validate, then promote.
   b. Recalculate error budget and notify Product + CS if SLOs breached.
4. Post-incident (within 48h)
   a. Open incident ticket with timeline and root cause hypotheses.
   b. Assign postmortem owner and schedule a blameless review.

5) Retrospectives & continuous improvement process

- Postmortem cadence: all sev1 and sev2 incidents that cross error budget must produce a postmortem within 72 hours and a follow-up action list.
- Retro template: summary, timeline, impact (customers, revenue, ops hours), root cause, contributing factors, corrective actions (owner and due date).
- Action tracking: use Jira label platform-postmortem and track closure via weekly oncall review meeting.

6) 90-day roadmap (high level priorities)

Quarter goals (next 90 days):
- Q1: Improve observability depth for model routing (add per-variant metrics and end-to-end latency traces).
- Q1: Reduce alert noise by 35% via metric stabilization and tuning (target: reduce false positives from poorly labeled metrics).
- Q1: Stabilize autoscaler heuristics for burst traffic (goal: reduce scale-up time p95 by 30%).
- Q2: Implement per-customer capacity reservations for Dedicated offering (pilot with 2 customers).

Planned milestones and owners:
- Add per-variant tracing to router-service (owner: serving-runtime) -- target 2026-03-15
- Dashboard refresh for control-plane & ingress (owner: observability) -- target 2026-03-01 (completed)
- Alert rule harmonization (owner: eng-sre) -- target 2026-04-01

7) Team wiki, onboarding, and links

Quick links:
- Platform playbook (full): /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-and-services-playbook-2026.json
- Runbooks repo: git@repo/platform-runbooks.git
- Grafana templates: git@repo/grafana-templates.git
- Prometheus rules repo: git@repo/prometheus-rules.git
- Oncall schedule (rota): https://oncall.internal/rota/platform

New engineer checklist:
1. Read this page and the platform playbook.
2. Join #platform-oncall and #platform-dashboards.
3. Request Grafana and Prometheus read/write tokens (follow people-ops access process).
4. Shadow oncall for one week and complete 2 runbook-driven drills.

Appendix A - escalation matrix (condensed)
- Primary oncall -> Secondary oncall (10m) -> Team lead (20m) -> Eng SRE (45m) -> CTO (2h)

Appendix B - sample Prometheus alert rule snippet
- alert: ControlPlaneHigh5xx
  expr: |
    increase(http_server_errors_total{job="control-api"}[5m]) > 50
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: "sev1"
  annotations:
    summary: "Control API 5xx spike"
    runbook: "https://runbooks.internal/runbook-control-api-5xx"

Appendix C - runbook storage and ownership
- All runbooks live in git repo: git@repo/platform-runbooks.git and use the naming convention above. Owner metadata must be present in the runbook header.

Changes and maintenance
- This page is reviewed quarterly by the Platform and Eng SRE leads. Major changes (process or SLA) must go through a review doc and be approved by the Observability Guild and Eng SRE manager.

If you have corrections or additions, open a PR against this wiki page source or contact the page owner (Ava Chen).
